transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, uh… I’m here because things at work have gotten strange since I got that county safety award. I’m a transportation inspector, and ever since then, certain people have been taking my inspection reports and kind of twisting them around, like making it look like I’m cutting corners or maybe doing something crooked.

And it’s not just one thing, you know? They’ll ask these pointed budget questions, like they already decided there’s something wrong. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I know what normal review looks like. I’ve been doing this long enough. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me. Anyway, that’s why I came in.
Do you think these people are actually out to get you?

Yeah, I mean… “out to get me” sounds kind of dramatic, but yes, I think certain people at work are trying to set me up, or at least make me look bad. Ever since that county safety award, my reports have been coming back all twisted around, like they’re trying to make it seem like I’m cutting corners or doing something crooked.

And then the budget questions—those aren’t normal questions, not the way they ask them. My supervisor says it’s just review, but I know what a normal review looks like. It feels coordinated, like they want to discredit me.
Do you think these people would be doing this to you if you hadn't received the county safety award?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, before that award, things were normal enough—work is work, people complain about road closures and budgets and all that, but it wasn’t like this.

After the award, that’s when my reports started coming back with weird comments, like someone was reading them just to find a way to make me look sloppy. And the budget questions, too… they ask them like they already think I’m doing something wrong. It reminds me of when my cousin got promoted at the warehouse and suddenly everyone had opinions about how he got there—people get funny when somebody gets recognized.

So, yeah, I think the award put a target on me. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I know the difference. It feels coordinated.
Do you think anyone outside of your workplace is involved in this effort to discredit you?

Outside work? I mean… I don’t know for sure. The main thing I can see is people at work, because that’s where my reports are getting picked apart and where those budget questions are coming from.

But sometimes it feels like it could be wider than that, because transportation stuff gets around—county meetings, contractors, people talking. My uncle used to say once your name is on something public, everybody thinks they know your business. But I don’t have, like, a name of someone outside the office.

What I know is ever since that safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports, making it look like I’m cutting corners or doing something crooked. My supervisor says it’s normal review, but it doesn’t feel normal. It feels coordinated.
Do you think these people at work are specifically targeting you because of who you are, rather than just your actions or the award?

I don’t know if it’s because of, like, who I am as a person exactly. I mean… maybe partly, because I’m the one who got the county safety award, so now my name is the one people remember.

But what I’m saying is, ever since that award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports, asking these pointed budget questions like I’m doing something crooked. And my supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I’ve been doing this job long enough to know when something feels off.

It’s like when you’re driving the same road every day and then one day there’s a cone moved just enough that you know somebody’s been there messing with things. That’s how it feels. Coordinated. Like they’re trying to discredit me.
Do you think these people would still be trying to discredit you if you hadn't done anything differently after receiving the county safety award?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, it wasn’t like I changed how I do inspections after the award. Same roads, same forms, same way I’ve always written things up.

But after that award, suddenly certain people at work started twisting my inspection reports, making little things look bigger than they were, and asking those pointed budget questions like I’m doing something crooked. It’s like when my dad used to say if you wash your truck too much, people assume you’re hiding a dent—doesn’t even make sense, but people get ideas in their heads.

My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I can tell the difference. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me whether I did anything different or not.
Have you noticed any changes or unusual events in your personal life outside of work since receiving the county safety award?

Outside of work? Not really in a big way. I still get myself up, get to work on time, do my inspections, keep myself together. I still go to church, same as before. I mean, I don’t just sit around letting everything fall apart.

It’s more when somebody starts bringing up those reports, or asking questions about spending like I’ve been doing something wrong—that’s when it gets under my skin. Because my uncle used to say once folks start counting your pockets, they’re not really asking about money, they’re asking what kind of man you are. And that’s how it feels sometimes.

But day to day, at home and church and taking care of myself, I’m managing. The problems mostly start around those reports and the budget questions.
Do you think these people at work are plotting against you personally, or is it just about your work performance?

I think it’s personal in the sense that they’re aiming it at me, yeah. Not just, “Oh, his work performance needs checking.” I’ve had my reports reviewed before. That’s not new.

But ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports, picking at budget stuff, asking questions in this pointed way like I’m doing something crooked. It reminds me of when my old shop teacher used to say a man can build a straight fence and somebody will still stand there squinting at it, trying to find a lean. That’s what it feels like.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I can tell when things line up too neatly. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to make me look bad, not just grade my work.
Do you think it's possible that your coworkers are not trying to discredit you, and that their actions have a different explanation?

I mean… I guess anything’s possible if you say it that way. But from where I’m standing, it doesn’t feel like some innocent misunderstanding.

Ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports, asking these pointed budget questions like I’m trying to pull something crooked. And my supervisor keeps saying, “No, it’s just normal review,” but I’ve been through reviews before. This feels different. It feels lined up.

Like my cousin used to work at a parts counter, and he said once somebody decides you shorted the drawer, every time you touch the register they watch your hands. That’s kind of what this is. They can call it policy or review or whatever, but I can tell they’re trying to make me look bad.
Have you felt like people are trying to discredit you at work every day since the county safety award, or are there days when you don't feel that way?

It’s not like I’m clocking it every single minute, no. I still do my route, I check what needs checking, I get my paperwork done. Some days I’m just focused on the job.

But since that county safety award, it’s been hanging over things. When those certain people get into my inspection reports, or start with those budget questions in that pointed way, then yeah, I can tell what they’re doing. They’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, but I’ve seen normal review before.

It’s like my uncle used to say about smoke in a kitchen—you don’t need flames in your face all day to know something’s burning. So maybe not every day the same way, but it’s there, and it keeps coming back lined up too neatly to be nothing.
Did you have any conflicts or issues with your coworkers before you received the county safety award?

Before the award? Not really—not anything like this, anyway.

I mean, work always has little stuff, you know, people arguing over routes or forms or who forgot to sign off on something. That happens anywhere. My dad used to say every workplace has one drawer that sticks, you just learn how to pull it right. But this… this started after I got recognized for that county safety initiative.

It’s been about a year now, give or take, since that award, and that’s when things started feeling different with certain people. Before that, I wouldn’t say there was some big conflict.
Did anything change in how your coworkers interacted with you immediately after you received the county safety award?

Yeah, pretty much right after. I mean, not like they all stood up and said something to my face, but the tone changed.

After that county safety award, certain people started looking at my inspection reports differently—like they were hunting for something. And then those budget questions started, real pointed, like I was trying to pull something crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I’ve had normal review before, and this isn’t that.

It’s like when my neighbor got a new truck and suddenly everyone had an opinion about where he parked it—people act like success is fine until it’s yours, you know? Anyway… yes, something changed. It felt coordinated, like they were trying to make me look bad.
Can you think of any specific action or event at work that you believe proves they are trying to discredit you?

Specific proof… well, I don’t have, like, a signed memo saying “let’s ruin him,” if that’s what you mean. People aren’t stupid enough to leave it lying around.

But the inspection reports, that’s the main thing. Since I got that county safety award, certain people go through my reports like they’re trying to find a loose thread to pull. Things that used to pass normal review suddenly get circled, questioned, sent back. And then the budget questions come in with this tone, like they’re hinting I’m doing something crooked.

It reminds me of when my cousin used to work at that parts shop—any time he did well, suddenly the manager “just happened” to check his drawer twice as much. Same kind of thing. You can tell when attention is routine and when it’s aimed at you.

My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I know what normal review feels like. This feels coordinated. Like they’re building a story to make me look bad.
Do you feel like they're trying to discredit you every time you're at work?

Not every single minute I’m there, no. I still do my job, I still check what I’m supposed to check. Like, you get focused on the clipboard or the route sheets and you’re not thinking about everybody’s motives every second.

But yeah… when my inspection reports come back all marked up, or when those budget questions start sounding like they’re trying to catch me in something, that’s when I feel it. Since that county safety award, certain people have been twisting things, making it look like I’m sloppy or maybe crooked. And my supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I know the difference.

It’s like—my uncle used to say, if the same porch light flickers every time you walk by, maybe it’s wiring, but after a while you start wondering who’s flipping the switch. That’s how it feels at work. Not every second, but often enough that I can tell it’s coordinated. They’re trying to discredit me.
Do you think your coworkers would be treating you this way if you hadn't noticed them going through your reports and asking budget questions?

I mean… if I hadn’t noticed it, maybe I wouldn’t be sitting here talking about it, but that doesn’t mean they weren’t doing it. That’s the thing. People act like because you notice something, you caused it somehow.

Ever since that county safety award, certain people started twisting my inspection reports, picking at them, and those budget questions got real pointed, like they were trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor can keep calling it normal review, but I know what normal review looks like.

It’s like when my neighbor had that fence put in and suddenly everyone was “just curious” about the property line. They weren’t curious before. So no, I don’t think it’s just because I noticed. I think I noticed because they were already coordinating it.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your coworkers' actions might be misinterpreted by you?

I’ve considered it, sure, because everybody keeps saying “maybe you’re reading into it.” My supervisor says it’s just normal review, like that explains everything.

But I know what a normal review looks like. I’ve been doing this job long enough. Ever since that county safety award, certain people started twisting my inspection reports, sending them back with these little marks like they’re building a case. And then the budget questions come in all pointed, like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

It’s like when my old shop teacher used to say, you can tell the difference between someone checking your work and someone looking for a reason to fail you. Same paperwork, different intention. So, yeah, I’ve thought about it… but I don’t think I’m misinterpreting it. It feels coordinated.
Have you ever felt like someone was out to get you before this situation at work started?

Before all this? Not really in any way that sticks out. I mean, people have little conflicts, you know—someone at work doesn’t like your tone, or back in school somebody thinks you’re trying to act smarter than them, that kind of thing. My uncle used to say there’s always somebody who wants to knock a nail back down if it sticks up.

But this situation, this really started about a year ago, after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. That’s when it changed. Before that, I wouldn’t say I felt like someone was out to get me like this.
Do you feel like you're more important or special since receiving the county safety award?

I don’t know if I’d say “more important.” I mean, the award was nice, sure. Anybody would feel good being recognized, right? You put in the hours, you catch things other people miss, and then suddenly there’s a plaque or a lunch or whatever and people clap.

But “special” makes it sound like I think I’m above everybody, and I don’t think that’s what it is. My dad used to say if you do a job right, don’t act surprised when somebody notices, but also don’t let it go to your head. I try to keep that in mind.

So… I guess I felt proud. Maybe more visible. Not more important exactly. Just like people were paying attention after that.
Do you think the county safety award has changed how you see yourself in relation to others at work?

I’m not sure. I mean, it changed how other people looked at me, maybe, or at least that’s how it seemed. As for how I see myself… I still show up, do inspections, fill out forms, drink bad break room coffee like everybody else.

It’s funny, that award plaque is actually kind of cheap-looking if you look close—my cousin got a bowling trophy once that looked nicer than that, and we all made fun of him because he kept it right on top of the TV. But still, when your name gets said in front of people, you notice who claps and who just kind of sits there.

So I don’t know if I see myself above anyone. I wouldn’t put it that way. Maybe I felt like I had proven I knew what I was doing. That’s different, I think.
Have you ever found any concrete evidence, like documents or recordings, that supports your belief that your coworkers are trying to discredit you?

Concrete like a recording? No, I don’t have, like, a tape of someone saying, “Let’s discredit him.” It’s not that simple.

But I’ve seen my inspection reports come back with wording changed, or things highlighted in a way that makes it look like I’m overstating problems or missing budget impact. And then certain people ask these pointed budget questions in meetings, like, “Why did you recommend that?” or “Did you consider the cost?”—but the way they say it, it’s like they’re setting me up to look crooked.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, everybody’s reports get looked at. And maybe on paper that sounds reasonable. But you can tell when several people are circling the same thing. It’s like when my brother used to “just ask questions” after he broke something in the house—he wasn’t curious, he was steering the blame somewhere else. That’s what it feels like at work. So no, not a recording, but there’s a pattern.
